title: DigitalOcean Pricing: Plans and Real Costs in 2026
summary: DigitalOcean pricing depends on which services you add. See which plan and services work for your specific usage needs.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Does DigitalOcean offer a free tier or trial credit?


No free Droplet is permanent, though new accounts have often been offered a promotional trial credit. The offer changes, so check the signup page for what applies on the day you register.


Treat any credit as a way to test your stack, not as a budget. Once it's spent or expires, the Droplet, database, and backups you leave running keep billing.


### Is DigitalOcean billed hourly or monthly?


Short experiments are cheap, because Droplets are billed per second with a 60-second minimum.


A Droplet that runs all month costs the listed monthly rate, and one you destroy after an afternoon costs only the hours it ran.


One catch: a powered-off Droplet still holds its disk and IP, so it keeps billing until you destroy it. Powering off isn't the same as deleting.


### Can I resize or downgrade a Droplet to cut costs?


Resizing up is easy, but downgrading depends on what you change. In the Droplet's Resize screen you can pick a "CPU and RAM only" option, which leaves the disk alone and lets you go back down later.


Grow the disk too and that change is permanent, so you can't return to a smaller plan. If you're unsure of your load, grow CPU and RAM first and leave the disk where it is. That keeps the downgrade path open.


### Does DigitalOcean charge for inbound traffic?


No. Inbound traffic to a Droplet isn't billed. What counts is outbound transfer, and each Droplet comes with an allowance that is pooled across your account. Overage on outbound traffic is charged per unit.


For a typical small site that serves pages and receives uploads, the allowance is rarely the issue.


It becomes a real line item when you serve large files, video, or downloads, so check your outbound usage before you add a load balancer or a second region that multiplies it.


### How do I set a billing alert on DigitalOcean?


Open the Billing section of the control panel and look for the billing alerts setting. Enter a dollar threshold and the email address that should receive the notice.


Set it a little above your expected monthly bill rather than at it. An alert set exactly at your normal spend fires every month, and you'll soon stop reading it.


Set a little higher, it fires when something unexpected is running, such as a forgotten snapshot or a managed database you meant to remove.
